title: Where are the arms and the vertex when a book cover opens?
description: A book cover is opened a little at first and then wider, in six cases. The cover and the pages below it are drawn as two rays, and the point where they start is found. Keeko's doubt, that the vertex is the open edge of the cover, is broken by the open edge that swings to a new place while the hinge stays still.
teaching_notes: One idea: an angle has two arms that start at one vertex, and the vertex does not move when the arms turn. Watch for students who pick the moving edge of the cover as the vertex.

source: Vidya opens the cover of her book in six cases (Case 1 to Case 6). Do you see angles being made in each of these cases? Can you mark their arms and vertex?
video_script.why: The child sees that the cover and the pages below it are the two arms of an angle, and that the hinge where they start is the vertex.
video_script.substitution: Draw the cover and the pages below it as two rays that start at the hinge.
video_script.anchor: the book of Ruhee, with its cover opened a little in Case 1 and wider and wider up to Case 6
video_script.wrong_answer: the vertex is the open edge of the cover
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the vertex is the open edge of the cover because that is the part that moves. The open edge is shown in three different places while the hinge stays at one place, so the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: The arms are the cover and the pages, and the vertex is the hinge

final_answer.value: Yes, an angle is formed in each case. The arms are the cover and the pages below it, and the vertex is the hinge where they are joined
final_answer.spoken: yes, an angle is formed in each case. The arms are the cover and the pages below it, and the vertex is the hinge where they are joined

names.Ruhee: the book's character who opens the cover of the book in six cases

never_show: the hinge named as the vertex, before the answer beat
maths_rules: An angle is formed by two rays that have a common starting point.
The two rays are the arms of the angle, and the common starting point is its vertex.
In the book, the cover and the pages below it are the two parts that turn, so they are the two arms.
Both arms start at the hinge, where the cover is joined to the pages, so the hinge is the vertex.
Slip: the open edge of the cover moves in every case, but the vertex stays at one place.
video_script.design: One idea: the arms turn and the vertex stays still. The book of the story stays on the board and its cover opens through the six cases. The wrong idea is that the open edge of the cover is the vertex.
